Differential item functioning

Source: R/dif.R
dif_test.Rd

Screens items for DIF between two or more groups.

Usage

dif_test(
  fit,
  group,
  method = c("lr", "mh"),
  match = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  p.adjust = "BH",
  purify = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  max_iter = 10
)

Arguments

fit

An irtfit object (or a response matrix / data frame when method = "mh" or match = "total").

group

A vector of group memberships, one per person.

method

"mh" or "lr".

match

"theta" (default when fit is a model) or "total".

reference

Reference group level for MH (defaults to the first).

p.adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment passed to stats::p.adjust().

purify

Iteratively purify the matching score (MH, and LR with match = "total"). Items flagged for DIF are removed from the total score and the analysis is repeated until the set of flagged items no longer changes (Holland & Thayer, 1988; Clauser & Mazor, 1998). The studied item is always kept in its own matching score. Not available with match = "theta"; use dif_irt() for purified IRT-based DIF.

alpha

Significance level used to flag items during purification.

max_iter

Maximum number of purification rounds.

Value

A data frame of class irt_dif, one row per item. With purify = TRUE, the column anchor shows which items were in the final matching score, and attr(, "purification") holds the number of rounds, whether the flagged set converged, and the flagged items at each round.

Details

  • "mh": Mantel-Haenszel for dichotomous items (two groups), matched on total score, with the ETS delta effect size and A/B/C classification.

  • "lr": logistic regression (binary items) or proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression (polytomous items), matched on the latent trait (EAP from fit) or on the total score. Reports uniform, non-uniform and total DIF likelihood-ratio tests and the change in Nagelkerke R-squared with the Jodoin-Gierl classification.

References

Holland, P. W., & Thayer, D. T. (1988). Differential item performance and the Mantel-Haenszel procedure. In H. Wainer & H. I. Braun (Eds.), Test validity (pp. 129-145). Erlbaum.

Clauser, B. E., & Mazor, K. M. (1998). Using statistical procedures to identify differentially functioning test items. Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 17(1), 31-44.

Zumbo, B. D. (1999). A handbook on the theory and methods of differential item functioning (DIF). Directorate of Human Resources Research and Evaluation, Department of National Defense.

Examples

set.seed(4)
d <- sim_irt(1000, 12, "rasch")
g <- rep(c("ref", "foc"), 500)
th <- attr(d, "truth")$theta[, 1]
foc <- g == "foc"
d$I03[foc] <- rbinom(500, 1, plogis(th[foc] - 1.2))   # harder for focal
d$I08[foc] <- rbinom(500, 1, plogis(th[foc] + 1.0))   # easier for focal
dif_test(d, g, method = "mh", purify = TRUE)
#> DIF analysis (Mantel-Haenszel, matched on total): 2 item(s) with B/C-level DIF
#> Purified matching score: 10 anchor item(s) after 2 round(s)
#>  item alpha_MH delta_MH statistic df     p class p_adj anchor

#>   I03    0.177    4.064   119.036  1 0.000     C 0.000  FALSE
#>   I04    1.039   -0.091     0.033  1 0.857     A 0.857   TRUE
#>   I05    0.946    0.131     0.075  1 0.785     A 0.857   TRUE
#>   I06    1.082   -0.186     0.231  1 0.631     A 0.841   TRUE
#>   I07    1.100   -0.224     0.282  1 0.595     A 0.841   TRUE
#>   I08    0.520    1.537    15.985  1 0.000     C 0.000  FALSE
#>   I09    1.046   -0.107     0.045  1 0.831     A 0.857   TRUE
